messages:
PagerBot: INCIDENT: continuous-batching alert — high cont-batch timeouts and KV cache eviction rate spike detected for prod-us-west-2. Auto-page to oncall.
Matt (Oncall): Acked. I'm on it. Seeing 5xx uptick and p95 latency climb on cont-batch routes. Dashboards: https://grafana/redwood/cont-batch (link)
Ashley (SRE): FYI I see KV cache size jumping then huge eviction bursts right after a config rollout at ~09:10. Evictions spiked ~40x. Did someone change batch defaults?
Ravi (Infra): That was my rollout — "batch-config-tuning". I pushed new defaults (commit abc123) to prod canary -> auto-ramped. I tested in staging but didn't hit this pattern.
Matt (Oncall): Ok. Quick mitigation options: rollback commit abc123, reduce max_batch_tokens, or disable cont-batch for heavy-seq routes. Need a quick safe path.
Jordan (PS): Customer impact: CS reports 3 accounts seeing retries and higher tail latency (alpha, beta, gamma). No confirmed SLA breaches yet but users are panicking. PS in contact.
Ashley (SRE): Proposed immediate hotfix: set max_batch_tokens=49152 (current = 131072), and lower max_num_seqs=64 cluster-wide for 15m. Also enable eviction-throttle to prevent stampedes. This should reduce per-batch memory and KV cache churn.
Ravi (Infra): Applying config patch now via infra-config API. Command I'm running:
```
curl -X PATCH https://config.redwood.internal/api/v1/cluster -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"continuous_batching": {"max_batch_tokens": 49152, "max_num_seqs": 64}}'
```
Pushing canary 10% first.
PagerBot: deploy-bot: config update submitted by ravi. CI checks OK. Rolling to canary (10%).
Matt (Oncall): Canary metrics: eviction_rate down ~50%, cont-batch timeout count down ~60%, p95 latency improves ~200ms on canary nodes. Looks promising.
Ashley (SRE): Proceed to ramp to 100%. I'll also add a short-lived rule to disable continuous batching for routes known to produce very long sequences (embedding/rlhf).
Ravi (Infra): Ramp complete. Also enabled eviction-throttle set to 0.2 to limit simultaneous shard evictions.
Ashley (SRE): Monitor queries I'm watching:
```
# KV cache eviction rate (5m)
rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])
# cont-batch timeouts
sum(rate(continuous_batch_timeouts_total[5m])) by (region)
```
Graphs show stabilization.
Jordan (PS): Confirmed with CS: latency and errors dropping for alpha/beta. Gamma still has elevated retries but much better than peak. I've messaged all three.
Matt (Oncall): Good. Leaving the mitigations for 30m then we'll evaluate. Action: open postmortem, assign owners.
PagerBot: Incident status: mitigation in progress — reduced customer impact. Monitoring for 15m stability window.
Ravi (Infra): Reaction :eyes:
Jordan (PS): Reaction :thumbsup:
Ashley (SRE): Initial root cause hypothesis: overly aggressive default max_batch_tokens (131072) increased per-batch token allocations, causing larger KV cache insertions and hot-evictions. Eviction storms led to cache misses/paging and backpressure, which amplified continuous-batching timeouts and request failures.
Matt (Oncall): Action items (short):
- Revert or make the tuned defaults behind a feature flag (owner: ravi)
- Add perf predeploy test that simulates seq length distribution (owner: ashley)
- Add alert for eviction_rate anomaly > 10x baseline (owner: eng-sre)
- Customer comms follow-up (owner: jordan)
I'll create the ticket and link here.
PagerBot: Incident mitigated by matt at 2309876590. Marking as mitigated; will wait for postmortem before close.
Ashley (SRE): I'll draft postmortem and timetable follow-up. Preliminary note: include config rollout checklist and a safe upper-bound guard for max_batch_tokens to prevent runaway defaults.
Matt (Oncall): Leaving a note for next oncall: if you see similar eviction pattern, rollback config and prioritize eviction-throttle.
Jordan (PS): CS will monitor customers for 24h and escalate if any regression.
Ashley (SRE): Good work all. We'll have a short blameless postmortem and publish learnings. :party_parrot:
